local_facts.claim: During July 2023, Phoenix recorded 30 consecutive days with highs of 110°F or more; Maricopa County had 42 Excessive Heat Warning days in 2023.
local_facts.why_it_matters: An uncooled Scottsdale garage exposes rollers, weather seals, lubricant, opener electronics, and battery backups to sustained high heat. An inspection should distinguish a heat-stressed opener component from a door that has become mechanically hard to move.
local_facts.title: Heat is a real load on garage-door hardware

local_facts.claim: On August 22, 2024, a thunderstorm cell moved toward Scottsdale; the National Weather Service documented uprooted trees, downed power lines, and local storm-spotter reports of more than half an inch of rain in 30 minutes over Scottsdale.
local_facts.why_it_matters: After a monsoon wind event, the door should be checked for shifted track, bowed sections, damaged weather seal, debris at the threshold, and opener or sensor problems before it is operated again.
local_facts.title: Monsoon wind can leave a door out of alignment

local_facts.claim: Scottsdale’s Historic Property Ordinance requires the Historic Preservation Commission to review and approve exterior alterations and demolition requests for buildings on the Scottsdale Historic Register.
local_facts.why_it_matters: This is not a citywide garage-door rule, but a visible door replacement or exterior design change at a registered property should be checked before custom materials, color, windows, or hardware are ordered.
local_facts.title: Some exterior changes require property-specific review

anchors.label: Contractor licensing threshold, aggregate contract price
anchors.detail: State law exempts unlicensed work only when the whole job, labor and materials together, stays under a thousand dollars and no building permit is required. Splitting a job into smaller contracts to stay beneath it is expressly prohibited.
